meta.title: Hausa Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 108 expressions · 38 greetings, 51 everyday, 19 exclamations · both directions
meta.desc: 108 Hausa expressions in three subdecks: 38 greetings and wishes, 51 everyday phrases and 19 exclamations and set formulas. Both study directions come as cards of their own: Hausa → English (see the expression, recall its meaning) and English → Hausa (see the meaning, recall the expression). This is not a CEFR level; it is the set phrases a learner needs whole, which a word list cannot teach, and nothing here is taught by any of the level decks. The greetings are the long exchange Hausa speakers open with (ina kwana? — lafiya lau; ina gajiya? — ba gajiya), the wishes for a journey, an illness, a birth and a death, and the leave-takings; the everyday phrases are the phrasebook sentences, and those for a man and for a woman are both given where Hausa tells them apart (kana lafiya? / kina lafiya?). WHERE THEY COME FROM: 8 of the 108, the Arabic religious formulas every Hausa speaker uses (salamu alaikum, in sha Allahu, alhamdulillahi), are English Wiktionary's entries and carry their tones and vowel length on a second line; the rest are glossed by Folio and carry no tone line, since a tone that no source states is not printed. A literal translation follows the meaning wherever it helps. THERE ARE NO PROVERBS: neither English Wiktionary nor the Tatoeba collection holds a Hausa proverb, and one written from memory would have no source. 47 of the expressions come with real example sentences from Tatoeba. There is no read-aloud button: few devices carry a Hausa voice. Sources. English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0), and Folio's own glosses. Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
